This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of The Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to allow the appeal, set aside the bail rejection order dated dated 8.4.2025 passed by learned Special Judge(SC/ST Act), Auraiya arising out of Case Crime no. 47/2024, under sections 420, 467, 468,
471, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(t), 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) SC/ST Act, at Police Station Kotwali Auraiya, District Auraiya.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the allegation is that appellant, who happened to be the owner of Gata No.828, sold the said land by executing a sale deed in favour of informant.
Later on informant came to know that land transferred in his favour, did not belong to the Gata No.828 rather it was a land of public utility and that too was a land belonging to Gata No.829.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that he is owner of Gata No.828 and has also sold the same land by executing a sale deed in favour of informant.
The sale deed is very much specific and it consists the description of Gata No.828.
Even the mutation in favour of informant has taken place.
All the allegations made in FIR by informant are fake and concocted.
Infact appellant himself was duped by informant who asked him to execute the power of attorney of the said land in his favour.
Appellant under impression that he was going to execute a power of attorney, executed a sale deed relying upon words of informant.
Informant himself has cheated him and appellant consequently has also filed a civil suit for cancellation of sale deed executed by him in favour of informant.
5. Learned AGA for State and learned counsel for informant have opposed the prayer for bail and have submitted that the land in question was owned by appellant.
Sale deed of Gata No.828 was executed in favour of informant and mutation proceeding in favour of informant has also been carried out.
But when informant verified the fact, he came to know that the land in question which was sold was not that of Gata No.828 rather of Gata No.829.
The said fact also finds mentioned in the report submitted by Halka Lekhpal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.
Report of Halka Lekhpal is sufficient to demonstrate that the boundaries mentioned in the sale deed executed by appellant is that of Gata No.829 rather than the Gata No.828 8.
Accordingly, the appeal against the order of rejection of bail is rejected.
(Anil Kumar-X,J.) November 7, 2025 Mukesh  Musarrat Ali vs State Of U.P. And Another on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107493563/
